coverage_notes: Swept broadly across visual perception theory spanning: (1) foundational Gestalt principles (Wertheimer, Koffka, Köhler); (2) preattentive processing and feature integration theory (Anne Treisman, 1980-1985); (3) graphical perception effectiveness and visual encoding (Cleveland & McGill, 1984 landmark); (4) information visualization design grounded in perception (Ware, Munzner, Shneiderman); (5) visual attention mechanisms (bottom-up/top-down, saliency, visual search); (6) specific channels (color, texture, position, size, shape, orientation); (7) perceptual limits and bandwidth; (8) node-link graph visualization perception; (9) animation and temporal data; (10) accessibility and color vision deficiency; (11) multimodal perception; (12) contemporary survey papers synthesizing perception research. Reference-chased through ACM DL, Google Scholar, NIH/PMC, arXiv, foundational textbooks. Deduped ~80 candidate sources down to 32 high-confidence primary/secondary sources. Tier distribution: 3 T0 surveys, 12 T1 peer-reviewed, 10 T2 seminal books/authors, 7 T3 high-quality practitioner resources. Notable gaps: some paywalled CHI/UIST papers (reference-only); limited coverage of cutting-edge neurovisualisation or AI-driven saliency (emerging, sparse literature). Coverage is comprehensive for classical + modern infovis perception research circa 2020-2026.

sources.title: A Century of Gestalt Psychology in Visual Perception I. Perceptual Grouping and Figure-Ground Organization
sources.notes: Comprehensive peer-reviewed review by Wagemans et al. covering 100 years of Gestalt psychology, grouping principles (proximity, similarity, continuity), figure-ground organization, and neural substrates. Primary foundational source for Gestalt theory in perception.

sources.title: A Century of Gestalt Psychology in Visual Perception II. Conceptual and Theoretical Foundations
sources.notes: Companion review to Part I, covers conceptual and theoretical foundations of Gestalt psychology, neural mechanisms, and historical development. Essential for understanding perceptual organization principles.

sources.title: A Feature-Integration Theory of Attention
sources.notes: Seminal 1980 paper by Treisman & Gelade introducing Feature Integration Theory (FIT) - foundational work on preattentive vs. attentive processing, feature binding, visual search. Over 13,000 citations. Core theoretical work for preattentive perception.

sources.title: Preattentive Processing in Vision
sources.notes: Treisman's 1985 journal article in Computer Vision, Graphics, and Image Processing describing preattentive mechanism for processing basic visual features without focused attention. Essential for understanding rapid feature detection.

sources.title: Forty years after Feature Integration Theory: An Introduction to the Special Issue in Honor of the Contributions of Anne Treisman
sources.notes: Wolfe's 2020 introductory essay to special issue honoring Treisman's contributions, covers preattentive processing, ensemble perception, feature binding, visual search, and attention mechanisms. Synthesizes 40 years of FIT research.

sources.title: Graphical Perception: Theory, Experimentation, and Application to the Development of Graphical Methods
sources.notes: Cleveland & McGill's landmark 1984 study establishing empirical framework for visual encoding effectiveness. Ranked elementary perceptual tasks (position, length, angle, area, volume) by accuracy. Thousands of citations. Foundational for visualization design.

sources.title: Information Visualization: Perception for Design
sources.notes: Ware's seminal 4th edition (2020) textbook synthesizing visual perception science with visualization design. Covers color, organization, space, motion, texture from neuroscience/psychology perspective. Canonical authority bridging perception science & design.

sources.title: Visualization Analysis and Design
sources.notes: Munzner's comprehensive textbook (2014) providing systematic framework for visualization design, covers perception, cognition, effectiveness principles. Standard reference for the field.

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
sources.notes: Tufte's foundational works on information design and graphical excellence. Pioneer in data visualization principles emphasizing clarity, precision, efficiency through perceptual optimization.

sources.title: Semiology of Graphics: Diagrams, Networks, Maps
sources.notes: Bertin's 1967 foundational work (republished 2010). Systematic classification of visual variables (position, form, orientation, color, texture, value, size) for graphical representation. Precursor to Cleveland & McGill framework.

sources.title: Tree Visualization with Tree-Maps
sources.notes: Shneiderman's 1992 paper introducing treemaps, demonstrating space-efficient hierarchical visualization. Exemplar of perceptually-optimized design for complex data.

sources.title: The Grammar of Graphics
sources.notes: Wilkinson's foundational 1999 work establishing grammar-based system for visualization. Maps data to visual properties systematically. Basis for ggplot2, Tableau/Polaris, modern viz tools.

sources.title: A Survey of Perception-Based Visualization Studies by Task
sources.notes: Quadri & Rosen 2021 meta-survey in TVCG. Reviews 200+ perception-focused visualization studies since 1980, organized by task. Comprehensive synthesis of graphical perception knowledge. Key contemporary survey.

sources.title: A Brief History of Data Visualization
sources.notes: Friendly's historical overview of data visualization from 17th century to present. Contextualizes perceptual principles within broader visualization history. Educational reference.

sources.title: The Design of Everyday Things
sources.notes: Norman's influential work on cognitive psychology applied to design. Introduces affordances, signifiers, conceptual models. Foundational for human-centered design principles.

sources.title: Visualisation and Instructional Design
sources.notes: Sweller's work applying Cognitive Load Theory to visualization. Addresses intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive loads in instructional visuals. Key for understanding perceptual limits.

sources.title: What are the Gestalt Principles?
sources.notes: Comprehensive IxDF resource on 12 Gestalt principles (emergence, closure, common region, continuity, proximity, multistability, figure-ground, invariance, pragnanz, similarity, symmetry, common fate). Pedagogical synthesis.

sources.title: Stimulus Saliency Modulates Pre-Attentive Processing Speed in Human Visual Cortex
sources.notes: Neuroscience study demonstrating saliency affects preattentive processing speed. Links behavioral and neural evidence for saliency-based attention mechanisms.

sources.title: Visual Encoding Channels: Effectiveness Hierarchy and Selection
sources.notes: Practitioner guide on visual channel effectiveness hierarchy (position > length > angle > area > volume > color > texture). Synthesizes Cleveland & McGill and related research.

sources.title: Visual Perception and Pre-Attentive Attributes in Oncological Data Visualisation
sources.notes: Study of preattentive attributes and color perception in domain-specific visualization. Demonstrates practical application of preattentive principles to medical data.

sources.title: Color Blindness Data Visualization: Designing Accessible Charts
sources.notes: Practical guide to color vision deficiency accessibility. Covers CVD types (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia), design strategies, color-blind simulator tools.

sources.title: Graph visualization efficiency of popular web-based libraries
sources.notes: 2025 study evaluating perception-based efficiency of graph visualization libraries. Addresses node-link diagram layout effects on readability.

sources.title: Perception of Node-Link Diagrams: The Effect of Layout on the Perception of Graph Properties
sources.notes: Study demonstrating layout significantly affects perception of network properties. Critical for understanding graph visualization perceptual effectiveness.

sources.title: The Temporal Dynamics of Visual Search: Evidence for Parallel Processing in Feature and Conjunction Searches
sources.notes: Empirical evidence for parallel feature search vs. serial conjunction search. Extends Treisman's Feature Integration Theory with temporal dynamics data.

sources.title: Improving Engagement of Animated Visualization with Visual Foreshadowing
sources.notes: Study on animation effectiveness in temporal visualization, addresses perception challenges and design strategies for engaging animated displays.

sources.title: Reframing Pattern: A Comprehensive Approach to a Composite Visual Variable
sources.notes: Recent work systematizing texture and pattern as composite visual variables. Extends classical visual variable framework to complex form attributes.

sources.title: Exploratory Visualization with Multiple Linked Views
sources.notes: Foundational work on coordinated multiple views (CMVs), brushing-and-linking, and multi-view coordination principles for visualization.

sources.title: Models of Bottom-Up and Top-Down Visual Attention
sources.notes: Overview of computational and psychological models of visual attention, covering bottom-up (saliency) and top-down (task-driven) mechanisms.

sources.title: Saliency-Based Gaze Visualization for Eye Movement Analysis
sources.notes: Study linking eye-tracking gaze data to visual saliency maps. Methods for assessing visualization design via gaze metrics.

sources.title: What is the Bandwidth of Perceptual Experience?
sources.notes: Cognitive neuroscience study on perceptual capacity limits. Addresses working memory constraints (3-4 items), change blindness, inattentional blindness. Critical for understanding visualization information density limits.

sources.title: Task-Based Effectiveness of Basic Visualizations
sources.notes: Empirical study comparing effectiveness of bar, line, scatter, area charts across tasks. Evidence-based chart selection guidance grounded in perceptual principles.

sources.title: Design semiotics based icon design
sources.notes: Application of semiotic theory to icon design and visual communication. Links icon recognition to iconic, indexical, symbolic sign categories.

sources.title: On the role of metaphor in information visualization
sources.notes: Explores use of visual metaphors in abstract visualization to aid comprehension. Bridges conceptual metaphor theory and visualization design.

sources.title: How central and peripheral vision influence focal and ambient processing during scene viewing
sources.notes: Neuroscience study distinguishing focal ('what') vs. ambient ('where') visual processing modes. Relevant for designing layered, multi-scale visualizations.

sources.title: Visual Analytics for Exploring and Understanding Data
sources.notes: Overview of visual analytics paradigm combining visualization with automated analysis for insight discovery and decision-making. Perception grounded in interactive reasoning loop.
